Q: How to secure encryption key A:

Keyring needs pywin32 to connect to windows credentials manager, So when packing the app into .exe, the pywin32 usually aren't packed properly. Thus, there is no way to deal with windows credentials manager. Therefore, to solve your problem, instead of save the password in a file, you could follow the next couple of instructions:

  • Make sure that Nuitka has imported the pywin32-cryptes using the following command :
nuitka --standalone --onefile --include-package=pywin32-ctypes --include-package=keyring.backends.Windows --windows-console-mode=disable your_script.py
  • Instruct yournapp to use backed.windows like:

import keyring.backends.Windows
keyring.set_keyring(keyring.backends.Windows.WinVaultKeyring())
# keyring.set_password(...)

Q: Pause shell script until user presses enter A:

Inside of bash you can use read -p, however this is not POSIX compliant according to shfmt.

TL;DR

printf '%s' "Press any key to continue..." && read

Full explanation & options

For POSIX compliance, you can use a couple different options:

Simplest option, and best one for general uses

printf '%s' "Press any key to continue..." && read

A bit more tight on what you can input.

printf '%s' "Press any key to continue..." && read -rsn 1 && printf '\n'

VERY tight, and handles input by processing the byte size of the user's input. Very unecessary, but included if anyone wants it.

printf '%s' "Press any key to continue..." >"/dev/tty"
trap 'unset _t' EXIT
_t="$(stty -g)"
stty -echo -icanon min 1 time 0
dd bs=1 count=1 1>"/dev/null" 2>&1
stty "$_t"
unset _t
trap - EXIT
printf '\n' >"/dev/tty"

Single line

printf '%s' "Press any key to continue..." >"/dev/tty"; trap 'unset _t' EXIT; _t="$(stty -g)"; stty -echo -icanon min 1 time 0; dd bs=1 count=1 1>"/dev/null" 2>&1; stty "$_t"; unset _t; trap - EXIT; printf '\n'

The only 'needed' snippet is:

read

This already handles input the way we want, so it can just be used alone.

All of these have been tested using bash and sh. Specifically (Shebangs):

#!/usr/bin/bash

And

#!/usr/bin/sh

Also tested using shellcheck:

shellcheck --severity=style --shell=sh --list-optional --color=always ./test.sh | bat

Resources

  1. man7.org --> read man page (POSIX)
  2. linux.org --> stty man page (POSIX)
  3. linux.org --> dd main page (POSIX)
  4. opengroup.org --> POSIX standard
  5. github.com --> sh formatted and syntax checker

Q: Repeat bash command for n seconds A:

Here's a simple way to run a short command for ~n seconds in pure bash, if you don't need millisecond accuracy. To note, like Gordon Davisson's answer above, a longer-running command will still continue to run after the specified time is up.

_timeout() { # USAGE: _timeout <duration> <cmd + args> EG. _timeout 10 blink_lights
    # reset bash special var SECONDS which counts up, then loop until >= duration
    SECONDS=0 ; until ((SECONDS>=$1)) ; do 
        ${@:2} # ignore first arg (duration) and print everything after
    done
}

Bonus with random duration within a designated range, and a roughly 50/50 nonzero exit - useful for testing

_random() { # USAGE: _random <min> <max> <cmd + args> EG. _random 2 5 echo hi
    local duration=$((RANDOM*(($2+1)-$1)/32767+$1))
    local exitcode=$((RANDOM%2))
    SECONDS=0 ; until ((SECONDS>=duration)) ; do
        ${@:3}
    done
    return $exitcode
}

Q: Python web scraping tool works on simple sites but fails on sites with anti-bot protections A:

Try replacing the standard fetch_page with the version using the cur_cffi library.

Install the library: pip install curl_cffi

Update the function:

from curl_cffi import requests

def fetch_page(url: str) -> Optional[str]:
    # Имитация реального браузера (TLS Fingerprinting)
    try:
        response = requests.get(url, impersonate="chrome120", timeout=15)
        response.raise_for_status()
        return response.text
    except Exception as exc:
        logging.error(f"Error: {exc}")
        return None

Q: Why is field injection discouraged in Spring, while it is encouraged in Angular? A:

Technically, it would still be possible for @Autowired to inject into final variables, unless they are final static AND inline-assigned (like constants). But injecting into a static variable is another thing of its own... So it's more of a 'contract' thing for @Autowired not to touch any final fields.

Also, the immutability aspect can be considered invalid, once someone uses Reflection.

And all the points attributed to inject() also hold true for @Autowired in Java.

As soon as you write tests, adding a context or writing the manual injection just goes along with the task (of writing the tests).

So in the end, just think about readability and maintainability of either way, considering how YOUR code is structured (inheritance vs constructors etc).
